title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer hysteresis + regional failover ordering
author: Marcus Patel
description: This hotfix addresses a production incident where the SLO enforcer could oscillate between regional failover decisions under rapid node recoveries, causing load-shedding thrashing and elevated error budgets. Root cause: an ordering/race between the enforcer's decision evaluation and the regional state reconciliation path combined with too-short hysteresis windows. Fixes: 1) introduce a minimum hysteresis window (configurable) to prevent rapid flip-flops, 2) make enforcer decisions monotonic by tagging decisions with a monotonic sequence id and rejecting out-of-order state transitions, 3) reorder reconciliation so that regional health events are processed before enforcer evaluation during a reconciliation tick, 4) add defensive checks to prevent double-apply of load-shedding thresholds. This PR includes unit and integration tests that reproduce a simplified oscillation scenario and a small canary in perf-canary to validate behavior under load. Checklist: - [x] Add minimum hysteresis window and config - [x] Add sequence id gating for decisions - [x] Reorder reconciliation path + tests - [x] Add unit + integration tests - [x] Run canary in perf lab - [x] Update release notes and Linear ticket comments Related: incident INC-2025-02-11, ENG-4391 (primary), ENG-4410 (follow-ups). Notes: change is intentionally conservative to avoid changing backoff math. We prefer a short hotfix now and follow up with a more aggressive scheduler rewrite tracked in ENG-4425.
